item.title: Ending currents of hyperbolic group actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a theory of ending currents for properly discontinuous isometric actions of hyperbolic groups on Gromov hyperbolic spaces, generalizing Thurston's ending laminations. Several natural generalizations are considered, which agree in the 3-dimensional hyperbolic setting but are otherwise distinct. We illustrate these invariants and their differences by several examples, including closed surface group actions on hyperbolic group extensions arising from Teichm\"uller theory and a geometrically finite action of a closed surface group on $\mathbb{H}^4$ with a single cusp that corresponds to a non-simple curve on the surface. We also discuss the conditions under which ending currents characterize geometrically finite actions, obtaining several equivalent conditions and some surprises, illustrated by an example of a geometrically infinite action whose ending currents are all supported on a single orbit of peripheral subgroups.
item.dc:creator: Yair Minsky, Tianqi Wang

item.title: Exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s as unions of two thickened circles
item.description: arXiv:2610.19263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an infinite family of non-diffeomorphic exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s, each of which is the union of two copies of a standard open tubular neighborhood of the circle, which intersect in a standard open tubular neighborhood of the wedge of two circles. This gives the simplest known decomposition of an exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$ into two open sets, making progress on Question 4.43 (A) of Kirby's 1995 problem list. The decompositions are obtained by studying fibered slice disk complements in certain Casson-Gordon homotopy 4-balls, for which we provide similar decompositions. We distinguish the $\mathbb{R}^4$'s using end Floer homology.
item.dc:creator: Sean Eli

item.title: Two non-semisimple quantum invariants of lens spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We calculate the chromatic spherical invariant $\mathscr{K}_{\mathrm{Rep}(H)}(L(p,q))$ of lens spaces $L(p, q)$ for arbitrary finite-dimensional unibalanced, unimodular Hopf algebras $H$. In the case of the index-2 Nichols Hopf algebra $\mathcal{K}_2$ and $q=1$, we find that the invariant of $L(p, 1)$ depends only on the parity of $p$ for $p\geq 1$. We also describe the duals $\mathcal{S_I}(M)^*$ of the admissible skein modules of handlebodies $M=H_g$ and of $M=L(p, q)$ for arbitrary tensor ideals $\mathcal{I}$ of a ribbon tensor category. In particular, $\mathcal{S_I}(L(p, q))^*$ corresponds with cyclic traces on $\mathcal{I}$ satisfying a property reminiscent of the modified trace condition.
item.dc:creator: Rhea Palak Bakshi, Mitchell Jubeir, Quinn T. Kolt

item.title: Relative knot concordance
item.description: arXiv:2610.19467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the relative-slice problem in $4$-manifold topology, we define for a knot $R$ the notion of a relative knot concordance group $\mathcal{C}_R$ and analyze the structure of its algebraic analogue $\mathcal{AC}_R$ modulo torsion. Using Milnor signatures, we show that $\mathcal{AC}_R$ has infinite rank for every $R$. We also show that any prescribed finite set of natural numbers can be realized as orders of elements in a single relative concordance group.
item.dc:creator: Vyacheslav Krushkal, Ryan Stees

item.title: The orientation-reversing minimal stretch factor problem in small genus
item.description: arXiv:2610.19828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the minimal stretch factors among all orientation-reversing pseudo-Anosov mapping classes of the closed orientable surfaces of genus two, three and four.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Dehornoy, Erwan Lanneau, Livio Liechti, Quentin Perroud

item.title: On local minimality of Hausdorff dimension for round limit sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.20358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address a question of Canary--Taylor and Canary--Minsky--Taylor for sufficiently symmetric compact hyperbolic $3$-orbifolds with totally geodesic boundary. We give sufficient conditions on the symmetries of such an orbifold to show that, among the complete convex cocompact structures on the interior, the structure with Fuchsian ends is a critical point (respectively, a strict local minimum) for the critical exponent. We also provide an infinite family of non-rigid examples fulfilling these conditions.
item.dc:creator: Sami Douba, Andr\'es Sambarino, Franco Vargas Pallete

item.title: Crystallographic quotients of Artin braid groups and torus bundles over flat $3$-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.20478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $n\geq3$, let $\overline B_n=B_n/[P_n,P_n]$ be the crystallographic quotient of the Artin braid group, with translation subgroup $\overline P_n=P_n/[P_n,P_n]\cong\mathbb Z^N$, where $N=\binom n2$. We prove that every compact connected flat $3$-manifold $M$, considered up to affine equivalence, is the base of a geometric torus bundle whose total space is a compact flat manifold with fundamental group a Bieberbach subgroup of some $\overline B_n$. More precisely, for every $n\geq n_M$, where $n_M\in\{3,4,5\}$ is an explicit optimal threshold depending on $M$, we construct a Bieberbach subgroup $\Gamma_n(M)\leq\overline B_n$ of dimension $N$ and a complete normal subgroup $K_n(M)\cong\mathbb Z^{N-3}$ consisting of translations such that $$ \Gamma_n(M)/K_n(M)\cong\pi_1(M). $$ We also determine which of the associated torus-bundle group extensions split: for the realizations constructed here, splitting occurs for exactly four of the ten affine-equivalence classes of compact flat $3$-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Ocampo

item.title: Minimal $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ Complexes of Rational Tangles via the Fukaya Category
item.description: arXiv:2610.20558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute minimal $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ complexes for oriented rational tangles, denoted $[\![\tau_{u/v}^{O}]\!]_N$, in terms of the topological Fukaya category of the $3$-punctured disk. This demonstrates that the complexes stabilize, allowing us to define a HOMFLY-PT homology for rational tangles.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan A. Higgins

item.title: Motion groups, Legendrian links, and non-trivial loops of embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2610.10804v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce, for an embedded Legendrian link~$L$ in a contact 3-manifold~$(M,\xi)$, the group of its \emph{Legendrian motions}. Analogously with the smooth case, we prove that this Legendrian motion group is isomorphic to the fundamental group of the space of unparametrised Legendrian embeddings. For all Legendrian knots in the standard contact 3-sphere, we characterise Legendrian motions in terms of contact mapping classes of the knot exterior. In an appendix, we give a short exposition of our techniques applied to the smooth case, comparing to the classical Dahm homomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Corrigan, Isacco Nonino

item.title: Index for a mutation loop
item.description: arXiv:2610.18940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the 3d-3d correspondence, we introduce an index $\mathcal{I}_g^\phi$ for a mutation loop $\phi$ of a quiver and an integer $g \geq 0$. We prove its integrality $\mathcal{I}_g^\phi \in \mathbb{Z}$ under certain conditions, which extends the integrality conjecture of Gang--Kim--Yoon for $3$-manifolds to the broader framework of mutation loops in cluster algebras. Our index also has an interpretation as the genus-$g$ partition function of a $(1+1)$-dimensional TQFT. We provide explicit computations for mutation loops of period one. In particular, in the case of the generalized Kronecker quivers, we give an explicit formula expressing the generating function of the indices for all genera $g$ as a ratio of polynomials. Altogether, we provide a new insight to the interplay between the geometry of $3$-manifolds and cluster algebra.
item.dc:creator: Tsukasa Ishibashi, Yuji Terashima

item.title: Enumeration of one-cycle signed chord diagrams and their duals for optimal Morse flows on closed surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optimal Morse vector fields on closed surfaces, i.e.\ fields with the minimal possible number of critical points (a single source and a single sink), are classified up to topological trajectory equivalence by one-cycle signed chord diagrams in Kybalko, Prishlyak and Shchurko (2018). We recall this construction and the associated duality, which corresponds to reversing the direction of the flow, in a unified encoding in which both endpoints of a chord carry the same label, and we make it algorithmic. We give an explicit traversal procedure that detects one-cycle diagrams, a canonical form of an equivalence class under cyclic shifts, reversal and relabeling of chords, and a construction of the dual diagram. On this basis we describe an algorithm that enumerates all one-cycle signed chord diagrams with a given number of chords, both for orientable and for non-orientable surfaces, groups them into equivalence classes, pairs each class with its dual, and identifies the self-dual ones. The algorithm is implemented in Python and archived in Zenodo; its output is validated against the Harer--Zagier numbers in the orientable case and against orbit-size counts in both cases. We also note that, when a one-cycle diagram is read as a cellular embedding of a one-vertex graph, its dual diagram describes the embedding of the dual graph.
item.dc:creator: Alexandr Prishlyak

item.title: Algebraic overtwistedness of contact $(+1)$-surgeries via augmented Floer theories
item.description: arXiv:2610.19333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that contact $(+1)$-surgery along a Legendrian $n$-sphere $\Lambda\subset(\mathbb{S}^{2n+1},\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$ with \[ \mathrm{tb}(\Lambda)\ne (-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}+1} \] has vanishing contact homology. In dimension three, this produces new examples of tight algebraically overtwisted contact manifolds, vastly extending the authors' previous results: If a Legendrian knot in $(\mathbb{S}^3,\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$ admits an exact, oriented Lagrangian filling that is not a disk, then contact $(+1/k)$-surgery on it is algebraically overtwisted and tight for every positive integer $k$. Our proofs use versions of symplectic cohomology and wrapped Floer cohomology defined by augmentations of a chain-level contact homology algebra.
item.dc:creator: Russell Avdek, Youlin Li, Zhengyi Zhou

item.title: The Weil-Petersson diameter of moduli space for large genus
item.description: arXiv:2610.19707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the large-genus order of the Weil-Petersson diameter of $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ for each fixed number of punctures: namely, $\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{M}_{g,n})\asymp\sqrt g\log g$. The main new ingredient is an integrated Ricci estimate for geodesics that minimize in moduli space and have thick endpoints, with no systole bound along their interiors.
item.dc:creator: Yunhui Wu

item.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19787v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.
item.dc:creator: Koji Fujiwara, Ryokichi Tanaka

item.title: Mapping class groups of solenoidal manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.20131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The goal of this work is to calculate the mapping class groups of solenoidal manifolds. We introduce the dynamical commensurator group associated to an odometer action, and develop methods to calculate the mapping class group using the dynamical commensurator. Our results generalize the previous results of Odden for the mapping class group of the universal solenoid over a Riemann surface, and of Bering and Studenmund for the pointed mapping class group of the universal solenoid over a compact aspherical manifold. We include a selection of examples.
item.dc:creator: Steven Hurder, Olga Lukina

item.title: Topological obstruction for Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish new restrictions on the virtual cohomological dimension of word hyperbolic groups admitting Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ ($p > q \geq 2$) or the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$. Our main result states that, if $P_k$ is the parabolic subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ stabilizing an isotropic $k$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^{p, q}$, a group admitting a $\{P_1,P_q\}$-Anosov representation into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $p$. As a result, a $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$-convex cocompact subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ cannot act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$. The main theorem also implies that a group admitting a $P_{\alpha}$-Anosov representation into the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $4$, where $\alpha$ is a short restricted root of $\operatorname{G}_2'$. As an application, we prove that the homogeneous space $\operatorname{G}_2'/ \operatorname{SU}(2, 1)$ does not admit any compact quotient.
item.dc:creator: Kewei Li

item.title: Completely parabolic surfaces are Veech
item.description: arXiv:2610.20566v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that completely parabolic translation surfaces are Veech, answering a question of Smillie-Weiss.
item.dc:creator: Inbo Gottlieb Fenves

item.title: Floer lasagna modules from link Floer homology
item.description: arXiv:2203.07650v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of Floer lasagna modules, which is inspired by the construction of skein lasagna module in [MWW19] by Morrison, Walker and Wedrich. Here we use link Floer homology instead of Khovanov-Rozansky homology. We give a description of the Floer lasagna module for 4-manifolds obtained by adding 2-handles to the 4-ball and we compute some examples.
item.dc:creator: Daren Chen

item.title: The fundamental quandle of ribbon concordances
item.description: arXiv:2602.20841v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe the fundamental quandle of a properly embedded surface $\Sigma$ (possibly with boundary) in $\mathbb{R}^{3}\times I$ and derive its presentation in terms of its motion picture. Our study is based on the topological definition of the fundamental quandle. We prove that a ribbon concordance $C$ from a classical knot $K_1$ to a classical knot $K_0$ gives rise to a quandle monomorphism $Q(K_0)\hookrightarrow Q(C)$ and a quandle epimorphism $Q(K_1)\twoheadrightarrow Q(C)$.
item.dc:creator: Eva Horvat, Luka Mar\v{c}i\v{c}

item.title: An embedding of spherical quandles into Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2603.29479v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct smooth embeddings of spherical quandles into conjugation quandles of Lie groups, where the ambient Lie groups can be chosen to be orthogonal, Spin, or Pin groups. Moreover, in dimensions $1$ and $3$, we compare our embeddings with those due to Bergman and Akita.
item.dc:creator: Ayu Suzuki, Kentaro Yonemura

item.title: Small Sets of Generators for Handlebody Groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.01003v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Wajnryb gave a finite presentation of the handlebody group $\mathcal{M}(V_g)$ and showed that it is generated by five elements for $g\geq 2$. Using his relations, we show that $\mathcal{M}(V_g)$ is generated by three elements if $g\geq 2$.
item.dc:creator: T\"ulin Altun\"oz, Celal Can Bellek, Emir G\"ul, Mehmetcik Pamuk, O\u{g}uz Y{\i}ld{\i}z

item.title: Minima of geodesic length functions for non-uniform filling systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.10344v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Kerckhoff proved that the geodesic length function $\ell_\Omega$ of a filling $\Omega$ on $S_g$ attains a unique minimum in Teichm\"uller space. Recent work of Ernesto Girondo et al. computed these minima for uniform fillings using the algebraic machinery of dessins d'enfants and Grothendieck-Belyi surfaces. We present an elementary optimization approach for $4$-regular topological uniform fillings, bypassing this framework. Furthermore, we analyze two special classes of non-uniform $4$-regular fillings using fat graphs and optimization techniques. We explicitly compute their minima and prove that in both classes, the minimum of these length functions is attained at a triangle surface.
item.dc:creator: Subash Chandra Behera, Shiv Parsad

item.title: Compressed primitivity problem in free groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.21499v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a fixed integer $r\ge 2$, we prove that the \emph{compressed primitivity problem} in the free group $F_r=F(x_1,\dots,x_r)$ is decidable in non-deterministic polynomial time. That is, for a \emph{straight-line program} $\mathcal A$ over $\{x_1,\dots,x_r\}^{\pm1}$ representing an element $g\in F_r$, the problem of deciding whether $g$ is primitive in $F_r$ belongs to $\mathsf{NP}$, with input measured by the size of $\mathcal A$. For $r=2$, we prove that this problem is decidable in deterministic polynomial time. We also show that, in every fixed rank $r\ge 2$, automorphic minimality of the conjugacy class of a compressed word in $F_r$ is decidable in deterministic polynomial time.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Kapovich

item.title: 6-valent vertex in the $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ web category and its categorification
item.description: arXiv:2608.21566v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define a $2\pi/3$-rotationally invariant 6-valent vertex in the $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ web category. When $N = 4, 5$, we provide a categorification of the 6-valent vertex using $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ foams and decompose the hexagon web into a direct sum of indecomposables. A similar decomposition is conjectured for $N \geq 6$.
item.dc:creator: Jernej Grlj, Mikhail Khovanov, Haihan Wu, Melissa Zhang

item.title: Property $(T)$ and nonlinearity of mapping class group quotients
item.description: arXiv:2609.12196v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a general method for proving Kazhdan's property $(T)$ for quotients $G/K_{[c+1]}$, where $G$ is countable, $K$ is a normal subgroup and $K_{[j]}$ denotes its lower central series. The method combines an affine realization of $G/[K,K]$, a contraction argument, and permanence for nilpotent normal subgroups. We apply this method to several classes of groups by means of homological representations. For the Torelli lower-central series quotients $\operatorname{Mod}(\Sigma_g)/(\mathcal{T}_g)_{[c+1]}$ for $g\ge3$ we show that they have property $(T)$ for every $c\ge1$. We also prove property $(T)$ for $\operatorname{Aut}(F_3)/(\mathrm{IA}_3)_{[c+1]}$ for every $c\ge1$, relating these groups to the tame nilpotent images studied by Lubotzky and Pak. Several other classes of examples are discussed as well. We also prove that the Torelli lower-central series quotients for $c\ge2$ are not residually finite, and thus non-linear.
item.dc:creator: Piotr W. Nowak
